description: "A recursive estimator that combines a model prediction with noisy measurements to track an evolving state."
term: "Kalman Filter"

## Simple explanation

A Kalman filter keeps a running estimate of a changing state, such as a robot's
position or a sensor reading, by blending the model's prediction with new noisy
measurements. It is widely used when uncertainty is important.

## Technical explanation

The filter maintains a state estimate $\hat{x}_t$ and covariance $P_t$. At each
step it predicts the next state using a system model, then updates the estimate
using a measurement $z_t$ and its uncertainty. The update is weighted by the
Kalman gain, which balances trust in the model versus trust in the noisy
observation.

The core steps are:

$$
\hat{x}_{t|t-1} = F\hat{x}_{t-1|t-1} + Bu_t
$$

$$
P_{t|t-1} = FP_{t-1|t-1}F^T + Q
$$

$$
K_t = P_{t|t-1}H^T(HP_{t|t-1}H^T + R)^{-1}
$$

$$
\hat{x}_{t|t} = \hat{x}_{t|t-1} + K_t(z_t - H\hat{x}_{t|t-1})
$$

where $F$ is the motion model, $H$ maps state to observations, $Q$ is process
noise, and $R$ is measurement noise.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Kalman filters are central in navigation, tracking, signal processing, and
robotics. They are useful when a system evolves over time and its sensors are
noisy or partial. The same idea is extended in many modern filters, including
variants for nonlinear systems.

## How it works

The filter assumes linear Gaussian dynamics and measurement models. It keeps a
state estimate and uncertainty, then uses the Kalman gain to decide how much to
trust each new measurement. In robotics, this allows smoothing noisy sensor
inputs into more stable estimates of position, velocity, and orientation.

## Practical example

A drone estimates its position using an inertial measurement unit and GPS. The
Kalman filter combines the motion model with GPS readings, weighting each one
according to its reliability. This produces a smoother and more accurate pose
estimate than relying on either signal alone.

## Common misconceptions

- A Kalman filter is not magic: it is only as good as the model and noise estimates.
- It is designed for linear-Gaussian systems; nonlinear variants are more complex.
- The filter is not a general-purpose replacement for machine learning or planning.
